extracted.intended_audience: NeurIPS 2025 reviewers and submitting authors (especially those who are both authors and reviewers)
extracted.subtask_description: Official NeurIPS 2025 guidance describing expectations, enforcement mechanisms, and sanctions for reviewers (particularly submitter-reviewers) to ensure timely and high-quality reviews across the main and D&B tracks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocal reviewing expectation / 'Submitting to NeurIPS Is a Partnership'
rubrics_metrics.description: Every submission needs to nominate a reciprocal reviewer from the authors; many invited reviewers also submit papers, creating a partnership between authors-reviewers and the conference. Reviewers—often authors themselves—must fulfill their obligation to provide thorough, punctual reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Framing: the system emphasizes a reciprocal system where authors expect timely, high-quality feedback. The post urges reviewers to think about reviewing as a partnership with NeurIPS that is essential to sustaining high quality and standards. This is an explicit community expectation rather than a procedural rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness requirement for assigned reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers who are also authors must complete their assigned reviews by the reviewing deadline; several reminders will be sent and those who are also authors and fail to submit their reviews will be specifically alerted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consequences for lateness are specified (see Reviews Withholding Mechanism and sanctions). Timeliness is enforced via reminders and targeted alerts to reviewer-authors. Implicit anti-pattern: submitting late or missing reviews despite being an author-reviewer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviews Withholding Mechanism
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers who are also authors (and their co-authors) will not see the reviews of their own submission(s) unless they have completed all assigned reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If reviews are late, reviewers (and their co-authors) will lose access to the reviews of their own papers until completion of their professional reviews (maximally until two days before the end of the authors rebuttal period). In the worst case, negligent reviewers and their co-authors will lose access to reviews on their own papers for the first five days of rebuttal. Reviewers will receive several reminders before the reviewing deadline; those who are also authors—and fail to submit their reviews—will be specifically alerted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review quality standard — substantive reviews (no 'placeholder' reviews)
rubrics_metrics.description: Area Chairs (ACs) and Senior Area Chairs (SACs) will flag any low-quality review, such as placeholder ones, regardless of whether it’s submitted on time or late.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of low-quality behavior include 'placeholder' reviews. ACs/SACs are empowered to identify and flag such reviews. The policy treats quality independent of strict timeliness: a timely but placeholder review can still be flagged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flagging and remediation process for low-quality reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: When ACs/SACs flag a low-quality review, the reviewer will be notified and required to address the issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an intermediate remediation step prior to sanctions: flagged reviewers get a chance to fix poor reviews. If significant problems persist after notification and are verified by the PC chairs and D&B track chairs, further sanctions may follow (see Desk Rejection Sanction).

rubrics_metrics.name: Desk Rejection Sanction for grossly negligent reviewer-authors
rubrics_metrics.description: Desk rejection at the meta-review stage is reserved as a last-resort sanction against grossly negligent reviewer-authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACs and SACs will flag low-quality reviews and notify reviewers; if significant problems persist and are verified by the PC chairs and D&B track chairs, the reviewer's own submitted papers may face desk rejection during the meta-review stage. This sanction is framed as a last resort and requires verification by higher chairs before application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of application across tracks
rubrics_metrics.description: Both the main track and the D&B (Datasets & Benchmarks) track will adopt these measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The policies (withholding mechanism, remediation, and possible desk rejection) apply to all submissions in both tracks; authors/reviewers in either track should expect the same enforcement and processes.
